messages:
sophie: alert from monitoring: private on-prem cluster for customer 'acidlabs' is showing sustained GPU queue growth and repeated autoscaler timeouts. first signs ~10m ago. stack: inference-pool.
ops-bot: [ALERT] GPU queue depth > 900 (threshold 200) for cluster acidlabs-onprem. autoscaler events: 12 errors in last 8m. paging oncall.
ryan: oncall here. seeing a steady increase in pending pods — autoscaler trying to provision but nodes stuck at 'provisioning' state. kubernetes events show cloud provider rate-limits.
maya: cs update: customer reported higher latency and 5% of requests returning 503s in the last 15m. they have a live demo running. customer impact: user-facing.
alan: logs from the node-provisioner show multiple timeouts to the storage attach step. looks like the provisioning step is hung, not kube-scheduler. sample log: ```2026-05-22T14:03:11Z provisioner: attach-volume timeout for instance-gtx-2 - retrying (attempt 4)```
irina: can we shrink batch sizes temporarily or redirect traffic to hosted region? how quick is fallback routing?
ryan: fallback to hosted requires policy change per-customer. short-term: reduce concurrency to avoid queue growth. pushing a temporary rate-limit on the route that goes to this cluster. executing: `redwoodctl routes update --customer acidlabs --max-concurrency 30`
ops-bot: action recorded: rate-limit set for acidlabs. preemptive mitigation in progress. :shield:
alan: autoscaler controller logs: ```E attach: volume attach failed: quotaExceeded: cannot allocate more volumes; API returned 429``` so it's hitting cloud quota/rate limits at provider layer. provisioning retries are backing up the queue.
maya: letting customer know we're investigating and have applied a temporary throttle. they asked whether we can failover some traffic to hosted models.
ryan: can do partial routing: we can route non-critical demo traffic to hosted model variant `rwd-gpt-medium` while keeping critical requests on-prem. planning to apply a route split 80/20.
alan: small config snippet to patch autoscaler (we should avoid restarts): ```kubectl patch hpa inference-pool -p '{"spec":{"minReplicas":2}}'``` but that won't help if provider can't create nodes. need to request cloud quota bump or pre-provision standby nodes.
infra-bot: recorded: cloud provider tickets need manual approval for additional GPUs in acidlabs account. current request queue length: 7. estimated time-to-provision for additional capacity: 25-40m under current load.
irina: handoff note for next oncall: if provisioning remains stuck after 30m escalate to infra team and request quota override. also consider emergency bypass: create a local standby pool of smaller instances (mixed CPU+lower-GPU) and run a lite model to reduce pressure.
ryan: performing the 80/20 route-split now. command: `redwoodctl traffic split --customer acidlabs --to-hosted 20`
ops-bot: [ACTION] traffic split applied. monitoring queue depth for changes.
alan: meanwhile I've triggered a manual pre-provision for 2 smaller GPU nodes (preemptible) as a stopgap. provider accepted but attach is still pending. continuing to watch attach logs.
maya: customer confirmed they see some decrease in demo errors, still elevated latency. appreciating speed of response.
deploy-bot: deploy note: we also have a canary for fallback model in staged deploy; if latency doesn't recover in 15m we'll failover non-sensitive calls fully to hosted canary.
irina: 20m check-in: queue depth dropped from 920 -> 260 after routing change and pre-provision. pending pods still 150. autoscaler still logs intermittent 429.
ryan: preparing incident summary for pager and next-hand-off. mitigation steps so far: 1) apply route split 20% to hosted 2) throttle customer concurrency 3) manual pre-provision of 2 nodes 4) opened cloud support ticket for quota override 5) monitoring dashboards pinned to #incidents.
alan: suggested follow-ups for postmortem: increase provider-side parallel attach limits in docs, add a provider-circuit-breaker to autoscaler to detect quota 429s and pause retries, add a pre-warm standby pool option for on-prem customers with large demo spikes.
maya: CS note: customer will wait for full restoration but asked for a timeline. please capture ETA in update.
ops-bot: [STATUS] 42m into incident: queue stable but degraded. ETA for full capacity restoration: uncertain (waiting on provider ticket). escalate if no resolution in next 40m.
irina: handing off to @ryan for next shift with pinned playbook in the thread. ry an, please add any outstanding actions.
ryan: handoff ack. outstanding: watch provider ticket, if quota bump granted cancel throttle and gradually shift traffic back. if provider takes >60m, escalate to eng-infra for emergency quota override or plan for longer-term hosted migration for this customer. posting handoff checklist now. :white_check_mark:
ops-bot: Incident updated and handed off to oncall ryan. Incident severity set to S2.
